answer: Recursive Matrix Pricing charges every new agent entity an entry fee calculated by the inverse density of its immediate cluster. When an attacker spawns nodes to manipulate a protocol signal, this density formula detects abnormal local clustering. The system demands an exponentially scaling native token payment from every newly registered node in that tight cluster before processing transactions. Every dawn, the protocol recalculates these node fees based on the graph topology. To anchor the ledger state during high volume, validators inspect the immutable onyx checkpoint hashes.
